newsitem.title: THAILAND: Democrats to win most seats in Thai election -poll.
newsitem.headline: Democrats to win most seats in Thai election -poll.

text.p: The Democrat Party of former premier Chuan Leekpai is set to win the most seats in Thailand's general election on Sunday, the respected Rajabhat Institute said in an opinion poll released on Thursday.

It predicted through a national poll of 140,000 voters that the Democrats would win 149 of 393 parliamentary seats at stake against 114 for the other front-runner, the New Aspiration Party, of outgoing Defence Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh.
The state-owned teacher's training Institute's polls are highly regarded in Thailand because the outcomes of several previous elections have been close to what it predicted.
Other newspaper polls have shown a generally mixed trend for the election, with some showing the Democrats ahead and others saying the NAP was in front in the close polls race.
The Krungthep Thurakij newspaper cited a private Special Branch police survey as saying the Democrats and the NAP were neck and neck in the race and would each win 125 seats.
Some political analysts said they were surprised at the wide margin given for the Democrats in the Rajabhat poll. "I had thought it was much closer than that," said one diplomat.
Charoon Choolap, the Institute's secretary-general, said the Chart Pattana Party of former prime minister Chatichai Choonhavan was set to come in third by winning 45 seats.
The Chart Thai party of outgoing premier Banharn Silpa-archa would come in fourth with 34 seats, he added.
"The past elections have proved that our poll is the most accurate and closest to the outcome," Sukhum Salaeysap, the Institute's poll co-ordinator, told a news conference.
"Past surveys have shown that there has been only a five percent margin of error from our academic and non-biased survey," he added.
In this election, 2,310 candidates from 13 parties are contesting the parliamentary seats.
No single party has ever won a majority in previous elections enabling it to form an administration by itself.
Traditionally, the party that wins the most number of seats in the election is given the chance to try to form a coalition government first.
Chuan and Chavalit have declined to work together whatever the outcome of the elections.

"If we win the most seats and have the right to form the coalition government I will give the priority to our opposition alliance," Chuan told reporters. The Democrats have an informal pact to form a coalition with the Chart Pattana and the smaller Seritham and Solidarity parties.
